side_notes.stated: Taken from a reviewed UniProtKB entry whose sequence is, letter for letter, this protein's. Each such entry is of another organism, named in the mark stated_in: it states the place of the same protein there, not in JCVI-syn3A. None of these statements rests on an experiment: each is made by a family rule or by similarity, as the mark evidence says.
side_notes.predicted: This tool's own reading of the sequence, not the output of an established predictor: UniProt's archive holds family signatures on these sequences and no prediction of membrane-spanning stretches. A stretch of 19 residues is read as membrane-spanning where its mean hydropathy on Kyte and Doolittle's scale is 1.6 or more and it holds no charged residue, or 2.2 or more with at most one. The window of 19 and the level of 1.6 are the usual reading of that scale (Paulet and others 2011 state it); the conditions on charged residues are this tool's, set against this organism's own proteins. A protein with such a stretch is placed in the membrane. A protein with none and no lipid anchor is placed inside, which includes proteins attached to the membrane's inner face. A lipid anchor is read from the lipoprotein signature (PROSITE PS51257, as UniProt's archive gives it; PROSITE's own terms are non-commercial, so its dependence is said here) where a hydrophobic stretch begins before its cysteine; such a protein is placed outside, because the lipoproteins of mycoplasmas are bound to the membrane and exposed on the cell's surface (Christodoulides and others 2018, said of mycoplasmas in general and not measured in this strain).
side_notes.by function: The sequence has a hydrophobic stretch, but the protein's class in the 2019 paper leaves no doubt that it works inside the cell: translation, transcription, the upkeep of DNA, sugar breakdown, the pentose phosphate pathway or nucleotide metabolism. Function is never used to place a transport protein.
side_notes.none: The sequence has a hydrophobic stretch that holds charged residues, and the protein's function is not known: nothing settles its side, so it is not placed.

essential.label: Essentiality
essential.note: Measured by transposon mutagenesis in this strain, then classified by the paper's model.

amount.label: Estimated copies in a cell
amount.note: An estimate: the measured share of the protein signal, scaled to the paper's estimate of 77,028 protein molecules in a cell. Given only for proteins that were seen.

added.label: Added for genetic manipulation
added.note: tetM and the yeast genes HIS3 and MET14: not part of the minimal genome.

class.label: Finer class
class.note: The 2019 paper's tertiary functional class, for laying out a district.

complex.label: Assembly
complex.note: Named outright by the genome record's product name: a ribosomal protein, a subunit of the ATP synthase or of RNA polymerase. Other assemblies are not marked.

segments.label: Membrane-spanning stretches read from the sequence
segments.note: This tool's reading; a count of stretches, not a topology. It can fall short, since a stretch that holds charged residues is not read.

lipid_anchor.label: Lipid anchor read from the sequence
lipid_anchor.note: The lipoprotein signature with a hydrophobic stretch before its cysteine. Such a protein is placed outside, unless a membrane-spanning stretch follows the anchor: then it is placed in the membrane. The signature is a profile of PROSITE, whose own terms are non-commercial (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0); where it matches was read in UniProt's archive, under UniProt's terms (CC BY 4.0), and nothing was downloaded from PROSITE.

at_start_only.label: Its one stretch is at the protein's start
at_start_only.note: The only stretch read begins within the first 12 residues. It may be an export signal that is cut off, and the protein would then sit outside and not span the membrane. Nothing read here tells the two apart.

evidence.label: What stands behind a stated side
evidence.note: From the reviewed entry that states the place: an experiment, a curator's inference, similarity to another protein, or a family rule.

where.label: Where within its side
where.note: A reviewed entry of another organism, with the same sequence, says the protein is at the cell membrane as a peripheral protein, without saying which face. Its side here is this tool's reading: inside, which includes the membrane's inner face.

stated_in.label: Stated in
stated_in.note: The reviewed entry of another organism, with the same sequence, that states the place, with its words.

unit_note: No protein has a unit: the atlas found none of the law inventory's units in this organism (data/proteins/atlases/syn3a.json).
